articles.title: The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless Gaming Headset With Infinite Battery Life Drops to $250
articles.summary: One of the best wireless gaming headsets is on sale today. Both Amazon and Best Buy currently have the Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro wireless gaming headset for Xbox, PS5, and PC for just $249.99 with free shipping, a savings of $100 off the retail price.
body: The one feature that undoubtedly makes the Nova Pro stand out amongst the crowd is the ingenious hot-swappable battery system. The Nova Pro includes two removable, rechargeable batteries: one to use in your headset and the other to remain charged and ready to go in a base station that doubles as a charger. This way, you get wireless freedom with zero downtime. Each battery lasts for up to 22 hours of continued use so you don't need to swap out too often.

The base station deserves additional mention. Not only does it charge your battery, it also features a clear and legible OLED display and a handy volume control knob. On the rear are USB inputs for connecting to your PC as well as an optional 3.5mm passthrough should you want to connect your speakers directly to the base station.
points: One of the best wireless gaming headsets is on sale today.
Both Amazon and Best Buy currently have the Steelseries Arctis Nova Pro wireless gaming headset for Xbox, PS5, and PC for just $249.99 with free shipping, a savings of $100 off the retail price.

articles.title: Level-5 Boss Addresses AI Backlash After Fans Hit Out at Game Reveal Showcase
articles.summary: Developer Level-5 has apologized for and explained its use of generative AI after fans spotted 'AI slop' in footage of games like Professor Layton and the Curious Village, DecaPolice, and more.
body: Concerns emerged following the studio's Nintendo Direct-style presentation earlier this week. Dubbed Level5 Vision 2026 II: Dreams, the show came with first looks at upcoming games, and it also happened to feature what fans suspected to be multiple examples of genAI.

Those who tuned into the 50-minute presentation spent more time talking about what they believed was evidence of AI use rather than the games, such as the Professor Layton remake, Yo-Kai Watch 2: Haunted Domain, and DecaPolice. The footage causing a stir is mostly limited to background scenes, but it's the fact that fans had to question Level-5 in the first place that's turned the situation into a full-fledged controversy for the Japan-based studio.
"You were a beautiful studio," another fan said. "Now you are nothing more than a disappointment to us. We don’t want this AI s**t."

Level-5 president and CEO Akihiro Hino, who also hosted the showcase with his own animated avatar, took to X/Twitter to calm the noise. His message was both an apology and an explanation, confirming that Level-5 did, in fact, use generative AI for some aspects of development.

articles.title: Blizzard's MOBA Is Making An Unexpected Comeback
articles.summary: At BlizzCon 2026, Blizzard Entertainment announced a new hero for Heroes of the Storm: Xal’atath. He’s coming to the game later this month, and could signal a larger return of support for the game.
body: World of Warcraft players will recognize Xal’atath as the Harbinger of the Void and a major player in the MMO’s recent Midnight expansion. Xal’atath will come to Heroes of the Storm's PTR next weekend, and is playable for those attending BlizzCon.

Xal’atath is the first new Heroes of the Storm character in nearly six years. The most recent release was Hogger in December 2020, a year after Blizzard ended active development on HotS. Blizzard indicated at BlizzCon that Xal’atath may not be a one-off; depending on player response, the company said it may consider adding additional heroes to the game.

Heroes of the Storm initially released in 2015 and was Blizzard’s answer to the multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) craze. The game featured heroes from across Blizzard's brands, with playable characters borrowed from Warcraft, StarCraft, Diablo, and Overwatch. While the genre had emerged in the custom game and modding communities of Warcraft 3, Blizzard’s official MOBA lagged behind games like League of Legends and Dota 2, never finding the same level of success as those titles.

articles.title: UK studio Bulkhead's Wardogs sells over a million copies and tops 350,000 concurrent players on launch day
articles.summary: Wardogs, the new tactical shooter from Derby-based studio Bulkhead, has sold more than a million copies and passed 350,000 concurrent players within hours of launching into Steam early access.
body: As IGN reports, the game's server queues filled up quickly as a result, with plenty of players unable to jump straight into a match due to server congestion.

"To cross a million copies sold as we launch into early access is mental," said Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer. "We've spent the last few months showing people exactly what Wardogs is, what it isn't, and at one point literally gave everyone ten reasons not to buy it. We didn't want people buying into blind hype."

He continued: "So seeing more than one million people choose to jump in and play the game at early access launch means a huge amount to all of us. But this is still early access. We've got things to fix, things we want to improve, and a lot more we want to build. The best thing players can do now is keep playing, keep telling us what they think and keep giving us those ridiculous Wardogs moments."
Wardogs' matches put up to 100 players into three-way fights for control points, mixing tactical shooting with vehicle combat, base construction, and destructible terrain.

articles.title: Scalpers are already reselling the sold-out Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 for £700+
articles.summary: Nintendo's new Legend of Zelda 40th anniversary Switch 2 sold out within hours of preorders opening, and scalpers are already scalping, with dozens of orders popping up on eBay for close to double its retail price.
body: Nintendo announced a new Zelda-themed console earlier this week, with Link-green Joy-Cons and a triangular pattern inspired by the golden glow of the Triforce. Plus, there's a similarly styled Switch 2 Pro Controller and carry case coming, too.

Retailers listed the console for preorder at around £435, £15 more than the standard Switch 2. All sold out almost immediately and Nintendo hasn't yet made the special edition available for preorder through its own store, nor said anything about restocking it before launch.

As GamesRadar+ reports, scalpers have since listed the console on eBay for anywhere between $700 and $985 (that's £520-£730ish). Some listings bundle it with the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake, even though Nintendo isn't offering any such bundle.
The Zelda-themed Switch 2 launches on 29th October, a week ahead of the Ocarina of Time remake itself, which arrives on 5th November.

articles.title: Heroes of the Storm gets first new hero after supposed death and 6 year wait
articles.summary: It's rare that a MOBA comes out, rarer that it manages to stick around, and perhaps rarest of all that it surges back to life after years on the backburner. While Heroes of the Storm never quite had its lights turned off, the constant downpour of new stuff you'd expect in a live service game did…
body: At today's Blizzcon opening ceremony, it was announced that Xal'atath, the Harbinger of the Void, will be arriving in the long-dormant MOBA as a new hero—its first since Hogger was released all the way back in 2020. It's the first truly substantial update since 2022, as the game has only received light-touch balance passes and bug fixes since Blizzard announced a shift to maintenance mode.

If you're unfamiliar, Xal'atath is a character from World of Warcraft's Legion expansion who started as a gnawing voice tucked away in the weapon slots of Shadow Priest players. More recently, she's become the villainous face of the current Midnight expansion.
It was also announced that another new hero would be revealed at some point in the future.
Xal'atath will arrive on the game's PTR this Monday, with a full release scheduled for Sep. 28. Follow the rest of today's Blizzcon news on our liveblog.

videos.title: PlayStation Ditched Hideo Kojima's Physint Over Budget Concerns and Missed Deadlines - IGN Daily Fix
videos.summary: More details are coming to light surrounding Sony's decision to part ways with Hideo Kojima's Physint project. According to reports, the game was already missing deadlines, was in danger of being overbudget, and was still years away from release.
points: More details are coming to light surrounding Sony's decision to part ways with Hideo Kojima's Physint project.
According to reports, the game was already missing deadlines, was in danger of being overbudget, and was still years away from release.
Sony has had a string of high-profile flops and cancelations—especially in the live-service space—so it seems like the company was looking to trim budget wherever it could.
In other news, another Sony-related property has popped up under a different name.
videos.author: IGN
